topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and frames the scope and challenges of learning the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamental principles, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core functions, historical naming conventions, and central biochemical significance of component C3 in complement biology.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biochemical mechanisms and threshold requirements of the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways that drive C3 activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how activated complement eliminates pathogens through opsonization, inflammatory signaling, and membrane attack complex-mediated lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the molecular mechanisms and regulatory factors that protect host cells from accidental complement activation and damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct disease phenotypes and clinical presentations that result from deficiencies in specific complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies and specific mechanisms used by pathogens like Staphylococcus aureus to circumvent complement attack.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of the adaptive immune system
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture on complement and announces the topic for the next session.
